full_statement:
Assume AC. Supply a discrete torsion-free nonelementary geometrically finite group $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$, in the finite-positive-radius-convex-neighborhood-volume sense. Write $\Lambda=\Lambda_\Gamma$ and $\Omega=\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\Lambda$. Assume all components of $\Omega$ are uniform quasidisks, with supplied orientation-preserving sphere maps of one quasiconformal bound. Supply representatives $D_j$, $1\le j\le m<\infty$, of all component orbits, their full stabilizers $H_j$, and their actual free holomorphic quotient covers
$$\pi_j:D_j\longrightarrow X_j=D_j/H_j.$$
For each $i$ put $D_i^*=\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\overline{D_i}$ and supply its actual free holomorphic quotient cover to $Z_i=D_i^*/H_i$. Supply stable finite-type compactifications of $X_j,Z_i$ with labeled punctures, cofinite disk Fuchsian models, their standard cusp data and the complete puncture/maximal-parabolic correspondence with primitive peripheral generators. Thus all input and opposite models, rather than only abstract topological surface types, are supplied. The genus and puncture counts may vary with the component. The empty case $m=0$, necessarily $\Omega=\varnothing$, means that both products below are a point.

Use the actual marked spaces $\mathcal T(X_j),\mathcal T(Z_i)$ of orientation-preserving quasiconformal markings, modulo label-preserving biholomorphism and homotopy extending jointly to the compactifications relative to the punctures, with the proved Bers complex atlases. There is a well-defined holomorphic map
$$\Sigma:\prod_{j=1}^m\mathcal T(X_j)\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal T(Z_i).$$
It is given as follows. Lift the coefficients of any representative input markings to the $D_j$, extend them $\Gamma$-invariantly to $\Omega$, set the coefficient zero on $\Lambda$, and integrate it to a normalized sphere map $f$. Then
$$\Sigma_i([Y_j,m_j]_j)=\bigl[f(D_i^*)/(fH_if^{-1}),\ \overline f_i^-:Z_i\longrightarrow f(D_i^*)/(fH_if^{-1})\bigr].$$
All puncture labels are transported as labels of the supplied $H_i$ quotient, even when distinct surface labels represent the same ambient parabolic class. The result is independent of representative markings and normalization. On chosen local input coefficient sections, the normalized realizing maps have holomorphic finite-point evaluations and every individual conjugated group matrix is holomorphic, without a finite-generation assumption on $\Gamma$.

At the reference point, identify intrinsic tangents and cotangents by the proved marked bounded-Beltrami duality. Tangents of $\mathcal T(X_j)$ are $B^\infty(X_j)/N_j$, cotangents are $Q(X_j)$, and similarly on $Z_i$. Here $Q$ consists of integrable holomorphic quadratic differentials, equivalently those with at most simple marked poles. Let $E$ denote the invariant extension of coefficient tuples just described. Then
$$D\Sigma_0([\nu_j]_j)_i=[(E\nu)|_{D_i^*}/H_i].$$
To state its complex-linear coderivative, choose, for each $i$, representatives $V$ of the $H_i$-orbits of all components of $\Omega$ other than $D_i$. Write $V=\gamma D_j$ and $K_{i,V}=H_i\cap\gamma H_j\gamma^{-1}$. The spot
$$W_{i,V}=V/K_{i,V}$$
embeds holomorphically as an open subset $\iota_{i,V}(W_{i,V})\subset Z_i$, and has the holomorphic unbranched covering
$$p_{i,V}:W_{i,V}\longrightarrow X_j,\qquad [z]\longmapsto\pi_j(\gamma^{-1}z).$$
For $q=(q_i)\in\bigoplus_iQ(Z_i)$ the coderivative is exactly
$$\bigl((D\Sigma_0)^*q\bigr)_j=\sum_{i=1}^m\ \sum_{\substack{[V]\in H_i\backslash(\pi_0\Omega\setminus\{D_i\})\\V\in\Gamma D_j}}\Theta_{p_{i,V}}(\iota_{i,V}^*q_i),$$
where $\Theta_p$ is the sum of inverse-branch pullbacks of a quadratic differential. Each sum converges absolutely in $L^1$ and locally normally, and is independent of all representative choices. The spots partition $Z_i$ up to a null set and satisfy
$$\sum_{[V]}\|\iota_{i,V}^*q_i\|_1=\|q_i\|_1,\qquad \sum_j\|((D\Sigma_0)^*q)_j\|_1\le\sum_i\|q_i\|_1.$$
The analogous formula holds at every marked input point, using its actual deformed domains and spot coverings. With maximum tangent norms on the finite products and sum cotangent norms, $\|D\Sigma\|\le1$. If at a particular point all its actual spot pushforwards obey one common bound $\|\Theta_p\|\le c$ with $0\le c<\infty$, then $\|D\Sigma\|\le c$ there. Separate strict bounds for individual covers do not assert a common $c<1$.

Every surface and map above has its inherited complex orientation from its sphere domain. An opposite quotient has the opposite boundary-side orientation to the corresponding input surface; it is not silently identified with that input complex surface. The pairing is the complex-bilinear $\int\nu q$, with no extra conjugation. If an antiholomorphic identification with the original oriented surface is imposed afterwards, that changes the holomorphic convention. Geometric finiteness, uniform quasidisks and the cofinite opposite quotient data remain explicit model hypotheses; none is claimed here for an arbitrary pared manifold.

actual_proof_anchors.quote: If $m=0$, the prescribed construction has coefficient zero everywhere, $f$ is identity, and both products are a point. All formulas are empty and hold; no area-zero assertion about the full-sphere lattice limit set is made. Hence assume $m>0$. Then $\Omega\ne\varnothing$, so [F2] gives $\operatorname{area}\Lambda=0$. There are at most countably many components, by choosing a different first element of a countable sphere base inside each. Also $\Gamma$ is countable: assign each element a basis neighborhood in the second-countable matrix group meeting this discrete subgroup only at that element. These injections and [A1] justify the countable orbit, sheet and component selections below. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

Let $B_j=B^\infty(X_j)$ be bounded Beltrami tensors, with its essential norm. Pullback through $\pi_j$ gives an isometric complex-linear map into the $H_j$-invariant tensors on $D_j$. In a sheet its formula is $(
u_j\circ\pi_j)\overline{\pi_j'}/\pi_j'$. Transport this tensor by $\gamma$ to $\gamma D_j$ and put zero on $\Lambda$. If another translate represents the same component, their difference lies in $H_j$, and pullback invariance makes the definitions equal almost everywhere. These are precisely [F1]'s invariant assembly operations; they define a bounded complex-linear operator $E:\prod_jB_j	o B^\infty(\widehat{\mathbb C})$ of norm one for the maximum product norm. Its norm is exactly $\max_j\|
u_j\|_\infty$, since each reference component is present and conformal coordinate factors have modulus one. The countable sheet and component covers transport exceptional null sets by conformal maps. The tensor is globally $\Gamma$-invariant, since the action permutes these component definitions and preserves their zero complement. If every $\|
u_j\|_\infty<1$, their finite maximum is less than one, so the full normalized solution $f^
u$ exists. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

For each $i$ we now establish the actual spots and coverings. Every component $V\ne D_i$ of $\Omega$ lies in $D_i^*$, since the two open components are disjoint and $\partial D_i\subset\Lambda$. The complement of their union in $D_i^*$ is $D_i^*\cap\Lambda$. Its image in $Z_i$ is null: use a countable quotient-chart cover, whose holomorphic local coordinates transport null sets, and [F2]. For each $H_i$ orbit of components choose $V=\gamma D_j$ and put $K=H_i\cap\gamma H_j\gamma^{-1}$. The restriction of the quotient cover $D_i^*\to Z_i$ induces an injective holomorphic map $\iota:V/K\to Z_i$: two points in $V$ identified by an $H_i$ element force that element to preserve their component, so it lies in $K$. Local covering sheets give an embedding onto an open subset. Different component orbits give disjoint embedded spots and all these spots cover the complement of the null image just identified. The map $p([z])=\pi_j(\gamma^{-1}z)$ is well-defined because $\gamma^{-1}K\gamma\le H_j$. It is a connected holomorphic unbranched covering onto $X_j$: over an evenly covered disc for $D_j\to X_j$, its lifts in $V/K$ are the $\gamma^{-1}K\gamma$-orbits of the original sheets, indexed by their subgroup cosets in $H_j$. Each is mapped biholomorphically to that disc. This proves the assertion without normality of $K$ or finite generation of it. Components and sheets are countable by step 1.1 and second countability. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

u$ extends quasiconformally to the labeled compactification. In particular $Z_i^
u$ is an actual object of $\mathcal T(Z_i)$, with its given $H_i$ labels, and [F4] supplies cofinite models at every such target. No conclusion that a general opposite quotient is finite type has been inferred: that reference datum was supplied. [F1, F2, F4, step 2.1, given, construct, algebra]

We prove the needed pushforward operation for any such covering $p:W	o X_j$. For an integrable holomorphic quadratic differential $r$ on $W$ and a relatively compact evenly covered coordinate disc $U$ in $X_j$, let $s_\alpha$ be its inverse sheets and form $\sum_\alpha s_\alpha^*r$. The sum of their absolute integrals over $U$ is at most $\|r\|_1$, by the conformal change of variables. On a smaller disc, the holomorphic mean-value bound in [F7] gives a summable bound for the suprema of these coefficients, with one fixed constant. Thus the series converges absolutely locally uniformly, so defines a holomorphic quadratic differential there. Reindexing sheets and using the tensor transition law proves compatibility of these sums. Partition $X_j$ into countably many measurable pieces lying in evenly covered discs; the corresponding nonnegative sheet integrals give $$\|\Theta_pr\|_1\le\|r\|_1.$$ Its integrability and holomorphy imply membership in $Q(X_j)$, with at most simple marked poles by [F5]. For bounded Beltrami $
u_j$ on $X_j$, the same absolutely integrable branch partition gives $$\int_W(p^*
u_j)r=\int_{X_j}
u_j\Theta_pr.$$ In coordinates the cancellation is explicit: $p^*
u=(
u\circ p)\overline{p'}/p'$ and $p^*(a(z)dz^2)=(a\circ p)(p')^2dw^2$, so their product transforms by $|p'|^2$. No regular-cover or finite-type assumption on $W$ was needed. [A1, F5, F7, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

The output is independent of representatives in their exact marked equivalence classes. Let $f=f^\nu$ and $g=f^\eta$ realize two tuples of equivalent markings. The input equivalences and exact identifications in [F1] give marked biholomorphisms of their complete conformal boundaries. Apply [F3] to obtain $H$ and $M=gHf^{-1}$ as described there. Because $H$ preserves $D_i$ and fixes its boundary pointwise, it also preserves $D_i^*$, so $M$ gives a biholomorphism $Z_i^\nu\to Z_i^\eta$. Its difference of markings is induced by $H|_{D_i^*}$, which commutes with $H_i$ and fixes $\partial D_i^*$ pointwise. In the supplied conformal disc uniformizer of $D_i^*$ it is a quasiconformal disc self-map commuting with the cofinite deck group and with identity circle boundary. Interpolation along hyperbolic geodesic segments is equivariant and continuous, and descends to a homotopy to identity. This is the puncture-relative homotopy of [F4], not merely an unmarked group equivalence: each labeled cusp subgroup is fixed; proper end preservation puts a sufficiently deep source horodisk into its prescribed target horodisk; geodesic segments between points of that horodisk remain in it. The entire homotopy is consequently uniformly deep at that puncture, proving joint continuity there, with each label fixed. This proves exactly the required equivalence of opposite marked targets. A different normalization of $f$ is Möbius postcomposition and gives an exact marked biholomorphism, so normalization is immaterial as well. [F1, F3, F4, step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

Pull a target quadratic $q_i\in Q(Z_i)$ back to each embedded spot, obtaining $r_{i,V}=\iota_{i,V}^*q_i\in Q(W_{i,V})$. Since the spots are disjoint and exhaust $Z_i$ up to a null set, countable additivity of the integrable absolute-value density gives the exact identity $$\sum_{[V]}\|r_{i,V}\|_1=\|q_i\|_1.$$ In particular for each fixed input label $j$, the series of all $\Theta_{p_{i,V}}r_{i,V}$ of that label over all $i$ is absolutely summable in $L^1$, by step 3.2 and the finiteness of $m$. It also converges normally on compact coordinate subsets, by the same mean-value bound applied to the individual holomorphic terms and their summable $L^1$ norms. Its sum is holomorphic, integrable and has at most simple puncture poles by [F5]. Denote this sum by $b_j(q)\in Q(X_j)$. Triangle inequality yields $$\sum_j\|b_j(q)\|_1\le\sum_i\sum_{[V]}\|r_{i,V}\|_1=\sum_i\|q_i\|_1.$$ These conclusions are valid for countably many spots; no bound obtained by maximizing separate strict covering constants has entered them. [F2, F5, F7, step 2.2, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

We prove holomorphy locally at the reference tuple without assuming a holomorphic quotient-family theorem. Use each supplied cofinite model to identify $B_j$ with its invariant disc coefficients. Let $ eta_j,\sigma_j$ be its Bers projection and local section, with coordinate variable $a_j$ in its auxiliary finite-dimensional Bers-coordinate space $A_j$. This space belongs to the opposite of that auxiliary Fuchsian double; it is not being identified with the geometric opposite space $Q(Z_j)$. Similarly write $ eta_i^-$ for the Bers projection for the reference surface $Z_i$, taking values in its own auxiliary coordinate space $A_i^-$. Restriction of $E
u$ to $D_i^*$ and descent to $Z_i$ gives a bounded complex-linear map $R_i:\prod_jB_j	o B^\infty(Z_i)$ of norm at most one; pullback by the fixed cofinite disc model is another isometric complex-linear operation. By equal-coefficient cancellation, the coefficient target of $R_i
u$ is marked-biholomorphic to $Z_i^
u$: the local maps from its intrinsic coefficient solution and from $f^
u$ have precisely the same coefficient on $D_i^*$. Thus in sufficiently small input and output Bers charts the map has the exact formula $$a\longmapsto eta_i^- igl(R_i(\sigma_1(a_1),\ldots,\sigma_m(a_m)) igr).$$ Every factor is a holomorphic map between the stated Banach or finite-dimensional spaces by [F4], so this is holomorphic. Shrinking the chart ensures its image lies in the target chart, since the sections pass through zero and $R_i$ is bounded. Separately, $E\sigma(a)$ is holomorphic into the invariant sphere coefficient ball. Apply [F6] to obtain holomorphic finite-point evaluations of its normalized solution and local holomorphic matrices for each $ho_a(\gamma)$. This is not an assertion of spatial conformality on a domain where the coefficient is nonzero. [F2, F4, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

The argument applies at every input point. Fix an arbitrary realizing map $f^
u$. Its new group is geometrically finite by [F1], its components remain uniform quasidisks with a bound multiplied by the one fixed dilatation of $f^
u$, and its component orbits are exactly the images of the old ones. Their marked quotient surfaces and the opposite quotients are precisely $Y_j$ and $Z_i^
u$ from step 3.1, with fixed puncture labels. They have the cofinite models and standard cusp data of [F4]. Rebase the input and output Teichmüller markings at these surfaces. For a small tuple of new coefficients use the new group's own complex-linear invariant extension and opposite restrictions. Step 5.1 gives the same holomorphic chart formula there. The resulting deformation composed with the fixed $f^
u$ represents the original global definition; the representative independence of step 4.1 proves equality of the output classes, not only equality of some conjugated groups. The chart transitions between these rebased marked spaces are holomorphic by [F4]. Hence these local formulas prove global holomorphy of the well-defined $\Sigma$. The same reasoning proves the asserted local representation analyticity at any base, with each individual group element treated separately. [F1, F4, F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

Its derivative has the stated intrinsic meaning. For arbitrary bounded $
u_j$, consider the actual coefficient paths $t
u_j$ near zero. By [F5], their tangent vectors are precisely $[
u_j]\in B_j/N_j$. On the opposite surface, step 3.1's marked map has coefficient exactly $tR_i
u$, not just a first-order approximation, since $E$ and restriction are linear. Hence its tangent is $[R_i
u]$ by the same tangent theorem. Differentiating the already proved factorization through actual marked classes gives $$D\Sigma_0([
u_j]_j)_i=[R_i
u].$$ This also proves independence of the input representatives modulo $N_j$. One must not assert without proof that a merely pointwise extension takes trivial infinitesimal classes to trivial classes; here it follows from the holomorphic marked map and its actual coefficient paths. Intrinsic cotangents are $Q(X_j)$ and $Q(Z_i)$ by [F5], whereas the auxiliary Bers coordinate spaces in step 5.1 play only their chart role. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

On a spot of label $j$, the target Beltrami representative $R_i
u$ of the derivative restricts exactly to $p_{i,V}^*
u_j$. This is the invariant extension rule of step 2.1, followed by the opposite restriction; both are the same holomorphic pullbacks on that spot. All integrals are absolutely dominated by $\max_j\|
u_j\|_\infty\sum_i\|q_i\|_1$. Partitioning into spots, using the pushforward pairing in step 3.2 and summing therefore gives $$\sum_i\int_{Z_i}(R_i
u)q_i=\sum_i\sum_{[V]}\int_{W_{i,V}}p_{i,V}^*
u_j\,r_{i,V}=\sum_j\int_{X_j}
u_j\,b_j(q).$$ By the intrinsic tangent/cotangent identification [F5] and the derivative formula in step 7.1, this is exactly the complex-linear coderivative identity $((D\Sigma_0)^*q)_j=b_j(q)$ displayed in the Statement. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy of that finite-dimensional cotangent pairing. Choices do not affect it, also directly: changing $\gamma$ by an element of $H_j$ leaves $\pi_j\gamma^{-1}$ unchanged; changing the $H_i$ orbit representative transports both the spot and its restricted quadratic by the corresponding deck transformation of the cover $D_i^*	o Z_i$. The branch sums are consequently the same under those identifications. Arbitrary ordering is immaterial by absolute $L^1$ convergence. All coefficient and quadratic transformations used here are holomorphic and have the displayed Beltrami phase; none is an antiholomorphic reflection. Thus the pairing is complex-bilinear and the formula has no complex conjugate. [F1, F5, step 2.1, step 7.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.2, construct, algebra]

On finite products, the dual norm to the maximum tangent norm is the sum of the intrinsic $L^1$ cotangent norms. The upper bound follows by the componentwise duality [F5] and triangle inequality. For its reverse, choose in each component a unit tangent making the pairing arbitrarily close to its cotangent norm, and multiply each by a constant phase to align the finitely many pairing values; their tuple has maximum norm at most one. This proves the norm assertion without a choice of minimizing coefficient. Step 4.2 then gives $\|(D\Sigma_0)^*\|\le1$ and hence $\|D\Sigma_0\|\le1$ by the same dual pairing. If every actual spot pushforward has a supplied common bound $c\ge0$, replace step 3.2's estimate by $\|\Theta_pr\|_1\le c\|r\|_1$ in step 4.2. The exact mass identity gives $\|(D\Sigma_0)^*q\|\le c\sum_i\|q_i\|_1$, and the dual pairing gives $\|D\Sigma_0\|\le c$. A countable family of constants all less than one can have supremum one, so no common strict bound follows just from their individual strictness. [F5, step 7.1, step 4.2, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

At any other marked input, use the rebased group and domains from step 6.1. They retain geometric finiteness and uniform quasidisks, and their component and opposite quotients have the required finite-type cofinite models. Their limit set is null by [F2]. All spot embeddings, subgroup intersections, cover maps and mass decompositions in steps 2.2, 3.2 and 4.2 apply to these actual deformed holomorphic data, not to a falsely declared holomorphic map between the old and new sphere coordinates. Applying steps 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1 in those intrinsic coordinates proves the same derivative, coderivative and norm assertions at that point. The labels are the transported supplied surface labels, kept distinct even if their ambient peripheral conjugacy classes coincide. This completes the construction and every stated formula. Establishing the model hypotheses for an arbitrary pared manifold, or a common strict bound over a varying family of covers or complex structures, remains an actual separate obligation. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.2, step 8.1, step 9.1, algebra] ∎

The current tangent/cotangent quotient proof, covering-pushforward proof, cofinite-model proof, full-sphere holomorphy proof, realization proof and metric/holomorphic-chart proof were read in full for this development. The local Bers and uniform-quasidisk marked uniqueness proofs had been authored and read in full; their actual marked fibers, auxiliary-coordinate conventions, commuting-map construction and puncture-relative homotopies were checked again. Their frozen bytes were not edited. The null-area, marked bounded-Beltrami duality, quasiconformal composition and Cauchy suppliers had been read in full during the preceding analytic and boundary development. The pushforward lemma is written out here, so no nonamenability hypothesis or unproved covering operator theorem is silently imported.
